clue.text: Licence form falsified and filled out with unsourced requirement

indicators.note: the reworked letters are filled out, stuffed with the next piece placed inside them
the word form is falsified, its letters doctored into a new order
the source of a word is its beginning, so unsourced drops the first letter

parts.note: a requirement is a need

explanation.surface: A doctored licence application padded out with some requirement that cites no source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Licence' reads as a permit but means liberty. 'falsified' rearranges the letters of 'form', and 'unsourced' drops the first letter of the requirement word.
explanation.definitionFit: Licence in the sense of liberty to act as one pleases is a synonym for being unconstrained.

clue.text: A bone brooch

definitions.meaning: the outer, thinner bone of the lower leg
a clasp or pin used by ancient Greeks and Romans

explanation.definitionFit: The calf bone and an ancient clasp share the Latin name, from the brooch shape the bone resembles.

clue.text: Previn certainly not all show!

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the conductor Previn didn't put on the whole show.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to reveal or display it, a synonym for show.

clue.text: Work at and learn to comprehend something needing to be filled in — a comfort to a setter?

parts.note: to do a task is to work at it

indicators.note: comprehend in its old sense of include or enclose, so the word for learn wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to get something is to learn or grasp it

parts.words: something needing to be filled in
parts.note: a blank on a form needs filling in

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's toil: grasping the gaps to be filled, then wanting comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is not the clue-writer but a dog breed, the Irish or English setter. 'comprehend' has its old sense of include or contain.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog blanket is a cover for a pet to lie on, and a setter is a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Folk artist who made use of tablets

definitions.meaning: Grandma ..., the American painter of rural scenes
the biblical prophet who carried the stone tablets of the law

explanation.definitionFit: The self-taught American painter and the prophet given the Ten Commandments on stone share this name.

clue.text: Put off and rescheduled hosting day in Paris

indicators.note: hosting means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
rescheduled suggests the word and has its letters rearranged

parts.note: jour is the French word for day

explanation.surface: A meeting postponed and moved to a new date while somebody was in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rescheduled' turns AND into ADN, which hosts JOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off a meeting is to suspend it until later, a direct synonym.

clue.text: An experience one's late in coming to

definitions.text: An experience one's late in coming to

parts.words: An experience one's late in coming to
parts.note: late here means dead, so this is what one comes to only once deceased, not something one arrives at tardily

explanation.walkthrough: 'late' reads as tardy but means deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Existence after death is something one reaches only once dead, which is the punning sense of being late.

clue.text: He thought a lot of 9, our setter in casual wear creation, coming to end of clue

indicators.note: in means the setter's name goes inside the clothing word

parts.note: jeans are casual clothing
Paul is another Guardian setter, so one of our setters
art is creation, as in a work of art
R is the resuscitation in CPR, the treatment that brings someone round so they come to

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word clue

explanation.surface: A setter in designer jeans thinks deeply about being, as the clue ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger could not account for the second R; the reading most solvers settled on takes 'coming to' as R for resuscitation, a loose abbreviation. 9 is BEING, and his chief work is Being and Nothingness.
explanation.definitionFit: The French existentialist philosopher wrote at length on existence, the subject of his major treatise on being.

clue.text: Not hardened, lacking cover, sunless

indicators.note: sunless means the letter standing for sun is removed

parts.note: without insurance cover

explanation.surface: A soft, exposed, uninsured person who never sees the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the standard abbreviation for sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Inured means toughened or accustomed to hardship, so its negative is a synonym for soft, not toughened.

clue.text: The very person to snoop around new swimmer

indicators.note: around means the word for snoop surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: to nose about is to snoop
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: Exactly the person to pry about a new swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Used for emphasis, as in that one and no other, the phrase means exactly that individual.

clue.text: Out of capital, journalist immediately starts getting on with life

indicators.note: out of signals that the following letters are taken away from the city

parts.note: Beijing is the capital of China
J is an abbreviation for journalist

indicators.note: starts picks the opening letter of the word immediately

explanation.surface: A reporter leaves the capital and at once begins getting on with life.
explanation.walkthrough: J and I sit side by side in BEIJING, so removing them leaves the answer. 'getting on with' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the sense of existence is a synonym for life itself.

clue.text: State position

definitions.meaning: a state of affairs or condition
a location or place, or a job

explanation.definitionFit: Both a condition of affairs and a job or location can be described by this one word, two synonyms.

clue.text: Want unpredictable result? How dull!

parts.note: want means lack, as in for want of

indicators.note: unpredictable says the letters of result fall in no fixed order

explanation.surface: Hoping for a surprising outcome and complaining how boring things are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unpredictable' turns RESULT into LUSTRE. 'How' just adds the exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacklustre has no sparkle or vitality, a straightforward synonym for dull.

clue.text: Combine temperature scale on exhaust

parts.note: F stands for Fahrenheit, a temperature scale
to exhaust a supply is to use it up

explanation.surface: Mechanic's jargon about combining a temperature gauge with an exhaust.
explanation.definitionFit: To fuse things is to melt or join them together, a synonym for combine.

clue.text: Top cleaner: for instance, good synthetic waste product

parts.note: eg means for example
sham means fake or synthetic
poo is a childish word for excrement

explanation.surface: An advert for a superb cleaner made from a synthetic by-product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is not a superlative but the head, the part this cleans.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is washed on the top of the head, and this is a hair wash made with egg.

clue.text: Working round obsession to wear cape leads to oblivion

indicators.note: to wear is to have on the outside, so the cape wraps around what has been built

parts.note: ness is a word for a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbours

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: working machinery is said to be on
someone with a thing about something has an obsession

explanation.surface: An obsession with wearing a cape at work ends in oblivion.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'round' wraps the working word about the obsession, then 'to wear' puts that whole inside the cape. 'leads to' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Nothingness is a state of non-existence, which is what oblivion means.

clue.text: Type of junior student's note attached to end of sensory organ

parts.note: a third is a musical interval, taken here as the note a third above

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word sensory

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A junior student's note stuck to the end of a sensory organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sensory organ' looks like one piece but splits: Y from 'sensory', then EAR. In US high schools and colleges, a junior is in the third year.
explanation.definitionFit: In a four-year American course the junior is the student in the penultimate year, so the third.

clue.text: They have the same atomic number (one), therefore, added to drinks

definitions.text: They have the same atomic number

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
so means therefore
to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: same atomic number, plus drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Variants of an element share the proton count but differ in neutrons, which is the scientific definition.

clue.text: It's deceitful — "hat", if clued cryptically?

parts.note: these words are what a cryptic clue reading BAD (an anagram signal) and FAITH would give, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a word clued cryptically is a deceitful trick.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: BAD as an anagram signal acting on FAITH gives 'hat, if'. 'clued cryptically' tells you to read the answer as a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting dishonestly, with intent to deceive, is a recognised idiom in law and ethics.

clue.text: Alien, else Spanish, hourglass property?

indicators.note: alien means foreign or strange, so these letters are made strange by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A list of nationalities, extraterrestrial, other or Spanish, for some odd property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' looks like the first item in a list but it signals the anagram of ELSE SPANISH.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass figure is a curvy female shape, so the quality it has is a pleasing outline; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Disgust by dumping gold in natural gas location

indicators.note: dumping says one piece is dropped somewhere
in shows where the gold is dropped, inside the sea

parts.note: the North Sea, abbreviated N Sea, is home to Britain's offshore gas fields
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Revulsion at gold being dumped in a gas field.
explanation.walkthrough: The North Sea, between Britain and Scandinavia, is a major source of natural gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is sickness, and figuratively strong revulsion or loathing, a synonym for disgust.

clue.text: See 6
President: "I appreciate that newspaper"

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank you
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A president thanking someone for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thanks; the FT is the Financial Times, a London daily.
explanation.definitionFit: William Howard Taft was the twenty-seventh American head of state, an example.

clue.text: African city tot is given a yeast cake

parts.note: to tot up is to add
a baba is a rich yeast cake, often soaked in rum

explanation.surface: A small child is handed a yeasted cake in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child but is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital of Ethiopia, an example of a city in Africa.

clue.text: After short time, one gets into one's pilgrim garment

indicators.note: gets into means these letters go inside the following piece

parts.note: one is, contracted, becomes I'm

indicators.note: after means the next piece comes behind the time

parts.note: hr is the short form of hour
a means one

explanation.surface: After a while, someone puts on their pilgrim's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: This white robe is worn by Muslim pilgrims to Mecca, so a specific example of a pilgrim's clothing.

clue.text: See 6
Soldier about to turn back warship

parts.note: a private is the lowest-ranked soldier

indicators.note: to turn back means the word for about is read in reverse

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A soldier about to retreat to a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was an armed private vessel licensed to attack enemy shipping, so a kind of fighting ship.

clue.text: Right away, here's to you getting advance

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: prosit is a toast, a German and Latin cheers

explanation.surface: A toast offered straight away while getting ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit a theory is to put it forward or propose it, a synonym for advance.

clue.text: Student of the sun absorbing extremes of temperature

indicators.note: absorbing means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: solar means of the sun
cold and hot are the extremes of temperature, abbreviated C and H as on taps

explanation.surface: A solar researcher soaking up very hot and cold conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: The extremes are not the first and last letters of 'temperature' but its two extremes, cold and hot, which are C and H on a tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or one who studies, a synonym for student.

clue.text: Reversing, say, a spacecraft's docking procedure

indicators.note: reversing means the assembled pieces are read backwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is signalled by say
the word splits as space plus craft's: space means room, and craft's tells you the docking is of a vessel

explanation.surface: Talk of reversing a spacecraft as part of its docking procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spacecraft' looks like one vehicle but splits in two: 'space' gives the room, and 'craft's' only colours the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooring a vessel is securing it at a berth, and the word also covers the place and fee for doing so.
